claims.text: Inducing short-range order in a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature mechanical strength.
Inducing short-range order will stabilize the alloy's thermoelastic behavior.
Short-range order improves strength and thermoelastic stability by reducing local lattice distortion and modifying dislocation interactions.
Cast HfNbTaTiZr is a bcc refractory high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast baseline is fully disordered, has a random atomic arrangement, and contains inherent lattice distortions.
Annealing at 800–1000°C for a suitable time can nucleate nanoscale short-range-order clusters.
An appropriately controlled anneal can induce short-range order without causing coarse precipitation or phase separation.
Nanoscale short-range-order clusters locally reduce lattice distortion.
Nanoscale short-range-order clusters act as pinning points for dislocations.
Short-range-order clusters stabilize the bcc matrix during thermal cycling.
Short-range-order clusters modify local bonding and stiffness.
Short-range order limits dislocation mobility at elevated temperatures and thereby reduces thermal softening.
Reducing elevated-temperature dislocation mobility enhances yield-strength retention.
Induced short-range order produces a moderated thermal-expansion response relative to a fully disordered structure.
The annealed alloy will have higher high-temperature yield strength than the as-cast disordered baseline.
The annealed alloy will have a lower or more consistent thermal-expansion coefficient than the as-cast baseline.
The annealed alloy will exhibit improved thermoelastic recovery in dynamic mechanical analysis.
The proposed mechanism applies to bcc refractory high-entropy alloys with low to moderate oxygen contents below 1 wt.%.
Annealing outside the 800–1000°C window or annealing excessively may cause precipitation or grain coarsening that masks benefits from short-range order.
